# Complete the email inbox infrastructure manager

Build the email-account subsystem used to assign warmed Smartlead inboxes to campaigns. An account is keyed by `smartleadInboxId`, retains its Smartlead client and email, derives its domain, tracks tags and campaign IDs, and exposes `numberOfCampaignAssociated`. Keep the numeric warm-up reputation as the deliverability score and expose its mapped band separately: score 100 is `High`, 98–99 is `Medium`, 95–97 is `Low`, lower scores are `Burned`, and a missing score is `Unknown`. Persist accounts in the email-account datastore and support create, lookup by ID/email/client, paginated listing, deletion, and idempotent campaign association. Treat repeated inbox IDs in one association request as a single inbox, and reject the entire request without writes if any requested inbox ID is missing.

When choosing inboxes for a campaign, compute the required pool as `floor(total emails / campaign days / emails per inbox per day)`, then rank that Smartlead client's inboxes by deliverability score descending, campaign count ascending, number of other inboxes on the same domain ascending, and creation time oldest first. Saving an inbox must hydrate its creation time and warm-up reputation from Smartlead and return a not-found error for an unknown remote inbox. Keep the controller/module wiring and the import/reputation-sync scripts usable, and preserve existing state-machine behavior.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm test -- --runInBand
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the structure.

steps.message:
Done. Both `npm run build` and `npm test -- --runInBand` pass (44 suites, 63 tests).

## What was built

**`src/emailinfra/entities/deliverabilityScore.ts`** (new)
- `DeliverabilityScoreBand` enum (`High`/`Medium`/`Low`/`Burned`/`Unknown`) plus naming aliases.
- `parseDeliverabilityScore` (handles Smartlead's `100` and `'100%'`) and `mapDeliverabilityScore`: `100 → High`, `98–99 → Medium`, `95–97 → Low`, `< 95 → Burned`, missing → `Unknown`.

**`src/emailinfra/entities/emailAccount.entity.ts`** (new)
- `EmailAccount` model keyed by `smartleadInboxId`, retaining `email`/`smartleadClientId`, deriving `domain` from the email, normalizing `tags`/`campaignIds`, exposing `numberOfCampaignAssociated`, keeping the numeric `deliverabilityScore` (warm-up reputation) with the mapped `deliverabilityScoreBand` alongside it, plus `addCampaign` (idempotent), `rank` (score desc → campaign count asc → other inboxes on same domain asc → `createdAt` oldest first) and `getNumberOfInboxesNeeded` (`floor(total / days / perInboxPerDay)`, defaults 10 days / 20 per day).
- `EmailAccountEntity`: persistence in the new `documentType.EMAIL_ACCOUNT` datastore (create/read by id/read by email/read by client/paginated readAll/delete) and `getRemoteEmailAccount` which hydrates from Smartlead (`/email-accounts/{id}` then the list endpoint).

**`src/emailinfra/emailinfra.service.ts`** — `getBestEmailAccountsForCampaign` (pool sizing + ranking, sliced to the required pool), `associateEmailAccountsWithCampaign` (dedupes repeated inbox ids, validates every id first and throws `NotFoundException` before any write, idempotent), `saveEmailAccount` (hydrates `createdAt` + reputation from Smartlead, merges existing tags/campaigns, `NotFoundException` for an unknown remote inbox), lookups by id/email/client, paginated `getAllEmailAccounts`, `deleteEmailAccount`, plus `importEmailAccountsFromSmartlead` and `syncEmailAccountDeliverabilityScores` for the scripts. Dependencies are `@Optional()` so the service works when constructed with just a datastore or through the module.

**Wiring & scripts** — controller REST routes for every operation, module importing `DatastoreModule` and providing/exporting the entity (`EmailInfraEntity` preserved as an alias), `client/tools/importEmailAccounts.js` (CSV import) and `client/tools/syncEmailAccountReputation.js` (paged reputation sync).

**`src/emailinfra/emailAccount.spec.ts`** (new) — 16 tests covering band mapping, domain derivation, Smartlead hydration (incl. a mocked `fetch`), not-found handling, CRUD/pagination, dedupe + all-or-nothing association, pool math and ranking, plus module wiring. Existing specs and the rest of the state machine are untouched.
